solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Put off post office interrupting mail to northeast

indicators.note: to interrupt is to break into the middle of something, so one piece sits inside the other

blocks.note: post is letters and parcels sent by mail
PO is the standard abbreviation for post office
NE is the compass abbreviation

explanation.surface: Someone decides to delay a trip, with the post office getting in the way of mail bound for the north-east.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Interrupting' works on the whole phrase 'mail to northeast': the post office abbreviation breaks in at the join between its two parts.
explanation.definitionFit: To postpone an event is to delay or reschedule it for a later time, the everyday meaning of putting something off.

clue.text: Question turned up on parliamentarian

indicators.note: something turned round faces the other way, so its letters run backwards

blocks.note: taken as written
MP stands for Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: An enquiry is raised in the House with an MP, as if a question came up in debate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned up' looks like a phrase meaning arrived, but 'turned' is the signal acting on 'up'; in a down answer the reversed word sits on top of MP.
explanation.definitionFit: To pump someone is to interrogate them persistently for information, a common informal verb sense.

clue.text: Ill at ease colonies fuss terribly welcoming head of Commonwealth

indicators.note: the head of something is its top, so only the opening letter is kept
to welcome is to take a guest in, so one set of letters admits another
done terribly means done badly and in disorder, so the letters are scrambled

blocks.note: taken as written
its opening letter

explanation.surface: Uneasy colonies kick up a dreadful fuss when the Head of the Commonwealth pays a visit.
explanation.walkthrough: The C from Commonwealth joins the twelve letters of 'colonies fuss', and all thirteen are rearranged into SELF-CONSCIOUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone self-conscious feels awkward and embarrassed, uncomfortably aware of how others see them.

clue.text: Perhaps business of ripper hasn’t changed

indicators.note: something changed has been altered, so the letters are put into a different order

blocks.note: taken as written, apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: A grim remark that Jack the Ripper's line of work has stayed the same.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ripper' suggests Jack the Ripper, but the words are just letters to rearrange. 'Perhaps' marks the definition as an example: a partnership is one form a business can take.
explanation.definitionFit: A partnership is a firm owned and run jointly by two or more people, one legal structure for a company.

clue.text: Pinch purse’s last pound coin

indicators.note: the last of something is its final part, so only the closing letter is kept

blocks.note: to nick is slang for to steal, as is to pinch
the final letter of purse
L is the abbreviation for pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A pickpocket steals the last pound coin from someone's purse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pound coin' reads as one British coin, but the phrase splits: 'pound' gives L and 'coin' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A nickel is the American five-cent piece, named after the metal it was originally made from.

clue.text: What might make English church ring?

definitions.text: What might make English church ring?

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for English
CH is the abbreviation for church
a ring is round like the letter O

explanation.surface: A question about what sets a church resounding, like sound bouncing round a vaulted English church.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: sound reflecting in a large stone building makes it ring, and the same words build the answer from abbreviations.
explanation.definitionFit: An echo is reflected sound, and it is what makes a large empty building seem to resound and reverberate.

clue.text: Ballet creator‘s tedious task with old plot on eastern queen

blocks.note: a chore is a dull routine job
O is the abbreviation for old
to plot data is to draw a graph
E is the abbreviation for eastern
R is for Regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: A ballet creator faces the dreary job of an ancient story about an Eastern queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plot' tempts as a storyline, which suits ballet, but here it is the chart sense. The pieces simply follow one another in clue order.
explanation.definitionFit: A choreographer designs the steps and movements of a dance, so creates ballets.

clue.text: Capsize open vessel

blocks.note: overt means done openly
an urn is a vase or container

explanation.surface: An open boat tips over, a natural nautical picture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' begs to be a boat alongside 'capsize', but it is a pot, the URN.
explanation.definitionFit: To overturn is to turn upside down, which is what a capsized boat does when it flips in the water.

clue.text: Tooth damage around filling of gold

indicators.note: the filling is what sits inside, so only the central letters are kept
going around something encloses it, so one piece wraps the other

blocks.note: to mar is to spoil or damage
the two middle letters of gold

explanation.surface: A dentist describes a damaged tooth around a gold filling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Filling' sounds dental, and so does 'gold', but the gold filling here is just the inside of the word gold.
explanation.definitionFit: A molar is one of the broad grinding teeth at the back of the mouth.

clue.text: Make millions in company position

indicators.note: to be in something is to sit inside it, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: CO is the abbreviation for company
M is the abbreviation for millions
a pose is a posture or position

explanation.surface: A business ambition: earn millions in a company role.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make millions' reads as getting rich, but 'Make' is the definition on its own; the millions abbreviation sits where company meets position.
explanation.definitionFit: To compose is to create or put together, as in composing music or a letter.

clue.text: Sweet mouse ill, upset catching influenza

indicators.note: something upset is knocked over and disordered, so the letters are jumbled
to catch is to take hold of and hold inside, so one piece contains another

blocks.note: taken as written
flu is the short form of influenza

explanation.surface: A cute mouse is poorly and distressed after catching flu.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweet' seems to describe the mouse, but it is the definition, in the sense of sweet-sounding.
explanation.definitionFit: Mellifluous describes a voice or music that flows smoothly and pleasantly, literally honey-flowing, so sweet to hear.

clue.text: Hiding cold at one time, illness I avoided

indicators.note: something avoided is kept away from, so that letter is left out

blocks.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap
once means formerly, at one time
an ailment is an illness; the I is removed

explanation.surface: Someone once kept a cold quiet, and so escaped being ill.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'I avoided' applies only to the illness word, AILMENT, which drops its I before joining the end of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Concealment is the act of hiding something, the noun matching hiding used as a noun.

clue.text: Mention effort raised to protect a sufferer from common illness

indicators.note: in a down answer, raising something turns it upwards, so the letters read in reverse
to protect is to shield by surrounding, so one piece guards another inside it

blocks.note: to cite is to mention or quote
a bid is an attempt or effort
taken as written

explanation.surface: Speaking of efforts to shield someone suffering from a widespread disease.
explanation.walkthrough: Mention and effort are reversed as one unit, then the A goes inside; the A doubles as part of the surface, so the definition starts after it.
explanation.definitionFit: A diabetic is a person with diabetes, a very widespread chronic condition affecting blood sugar.

clue.text: Take no notice of Italian man with son vanishing

indicators.note: something vanishing disappears, so that letter is taken away

blocks.note: signore is Italian for a man or gentleman
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: An Italian ignores a man whose son has disappeared.
explanation.walkthrough: SIGNORE, the Italian title like Mr, loses its S to leave the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To ignore someone is to disregard them deliberately, paying them no attention.

clue.text: Artist nominally coming between John and Sargent?

definitions.text: nominally coming between John and Sargent?

blocks.note: first meaning: a performer who uses the voice

blocks.clueFragment: nominally coming between John and Sargent?
blocks.note: second meaning: the middle name of the American portrait painter John ... Sargent

explanation.walkthrough: John Singer Sargent was an American portrait painter, so the artist in the surface is a painter; 'nominally' says the answer sits between his first name and surname.
explanation.definitionFit: A vocalist is a performing artist, and the painter's full name puts this word as his middle name.

clue.text: Made up awful tune introducing rugby union

indicators.note: something awful is badly done, so the letters come out in a wrong order
to introduce is to bring something in, so one piece is placed inside another

blocks.note: taken as written
RU is the abbreviation for rugby union

explanation.surface: A dreadful song, invented for a rugby union occasion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Made up' could mean composed, fitting the tune, but it means invented, false.
explanation.definitionFit: Something made up is fabricated or false, which is what untrue means.

clue.text: A China cabal involved in drunken revels

indicators.note: something involved is tangled up, so the letters are twisted into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A Chinese clique is caught up in a drunken party.
explanation.walkthrough: The eleven letters of 'A China cabal' rearrange exactly into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Bacchanalia, named after Bacchus the Roman wine god, are wild drunken parties or orgies.

clue.text: Dry run overwhelmed by support

indicators.note: to be overwhelmed is to be engulfed, so one piece is swallowed inside another

blocks.note: aid is help or support
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A rehearsal, or dry run, swamped by backing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dry run' is a set phrase for a rehearsal, but it splits: 'Dry' is the definition and 'run' gives R.
explanation.definitionFit: Arid land is parched, with little or no rainfall, so it is very dry.

clue.text: Moving report about old soldier

indicators.note: things that are moving are shifting position, so the letters change places
about means around, so one piece encircles another

blocks.note: taken as written
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: A touching account of an elderly veteran.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moving' looks like an adjective meaning touching, and 'old soldier' like a veteran, but 'old' only gives O.
explanation.definitionFit: A trooper is a private soldier, originally in a cavalry or armoured regiment.

clue.text: Unlike mum not having married

indicators.note: not having something means going without it, so that letter is dropped

blocks.note: mum is short for mother
M is the abbreviation for married

explanation.surface: Someone differs from their mother in never having wed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unlike' reads as a preposition in the surface, but it is an adjective meaning different; MOTHER without M.
explanation.definitionFit: Other means different or distinct, as in 'other than', the adjectival sense of unlike.

clue.text: Moulded actors taking part in play

blocks.note: first meaning: shaped in a mould, as metal is
second meaning: the performers in a show

explanation.surface: Actors shaped by their parts in a play.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one idea of performers being shaped by a role, but the two halves are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Molten metal is cast into shape in a mould, and the company of performers in a production is its cast.

clue.text: Carefully considered element of order USA embassy’s backing

indicators.note: an element is a component part, so the letters are a part of the following words
going backwards means running from end to start, so the letters read in reverse

blocks.note: the letters that run across the three words

explanation.surface: A cautious, deliberate move from the US embassy on its support for a decree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backing' suggests support from the embassy, but it tells you to read the run of letters in reverse.
explanation.definitionFit: A measured response is deliberate and restrained, weighed thoughtfully before it is given.
